Likelihood configurations

PCAT separates data likelihoods from transdimensional catalog postprocessing. Every transdimensional model produces a catalog at each retained draw. With the default boolcondcatl=True, final processing builds a condensed posterior catalog by associating recurrent supported spatial elements across those sampled catalogs. Optional matching to an external reference catalog follows this summary. Condensation and either kind of association are posterior products, not likelihoods. Set boolcondcatl=False to skip condensation. The current implementation does not spatially condense one-dimensional line, flare, or Keplerian catalogs.

Image likelihoods

The image workflow predicts counts in pixels from a source model, exposure, background emission, and instrument response. Point sources, extended emission, foreground light, and gravitational lenses are components of this one image likelihood, not separate likelihood families.

Data and pixelization

Set typedata="simu" for generated counts or typedata="inpt" for supplied data. For input data, strgexprsbrt identifies the surface-brightness or count-rate FITS input. Exposure can be constant with typeexpo="cons" and strgexpo or read from a FITS map with typeexpo="file" and strgexpo. PCAT converts the input to expected counts using the exposure and its configured units before evaluating the likelihood.

typepixl="cart" selects a Cartesian image. Set numbsidecart to choose its side length. boolforccart=True forces a square grid when pixel coordinates are supplied directly. typepixl="heal" selects HEALPix data and uses numbsideheal for its resolution. Fermi-LAT defaults to HEALPix. Other image experiments default to Cartesian pixels.

Poisson count-image likelihood

liketype="pois" is the default for count data. Omitting the data-only factorial, its log likelihood is

\[\log L_{\mathrm{Pois}} = \sum_i D_i \log M_i - M_i,\]

where D is the observed count map and M is the predicted count map. Gaussian image likelihood ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Set liketype="gaus" for the built-in Gaussian residual likelihood. Supply varidata as a per-pixel variance map. If omitted, PCAT uses the observed counts with a floor of one:

\[\log L_{\mathrm{Gaus}} = -\frac{1}{2}\sum_i \frac{(D_i-M_i)^2}{V_i}.\]

Source and lens components

Configure populations with typeelem and their true and fitted settings in dicttrue and dictfitt. Common image components include:

  • lghtpnts for point sources with sampled positions and fluxes.

  • lghtgausbgrd for extended Gaussian emission components.

  • lens for lens deflectors and their associated mass parameters.

  • clusvari for variable-width Gaussian components represented in an image count map.

  • typeemishost="sers" for a Sérsic foreground lens-galaxy light model; "none" disables this host-emission component.

  • boollenssubh=True to include lens-substructure deflectors where the selected lens configuration supports them.

The typespatdist or spatdisttype setting selects the spatial prior for each population. Source flux priors are selected with typeprioflux and bounded or customized with the corresponding per-element limits and limtparaelem where available. HST strong-lens examples combine a fixed macro lens and source/host light with a variable lens population for additional deflectors.

Background emission and exposure

Experiment defaults define the available background components. Override their templates with sbrtbacknorm in dicttrue or dictfitt. The listnamediff entry selects the diffuse components added to the model. Names such as back0000 refer to entries in the template list. boolspecback controls whether a background amplitude is shared spectrally or varies by energy bin. Fermi-LAT configurations can use a uniform component, a diffuse template, or the anlytype="bfun" background-function basis. Exposure controls how model brightness becomes expected counts and can be masked with listmask and typemaskexpo.

Point-spread functions

typeevalpsfn controls where the PSF is applied:

  • "none" leaves the source model unconvolved.

  • "kern" applies a local PSF kernel to supported point-source elements.

  • "conv" convolves eligible image components.

  • "full" enables both kernel evaluation and image convolution where supported.

The experiment selects a PSF profile family through typemodlpsfn. Current experiment defaults include single Gaussian, single King, and double King profiles. Supply profile parameters through psfpexpr in dicttrue and dictfitt. Set boolmodipsfn=True when PSF parameters should vary in the fit. Fermi-LAT can also use its energy- and event-class-dependent PSF scale fermscalfact. PSF and source-kernel options depend on pixelization and element type. Unsupported combinations should use typeevalpsfn="none".

Unbinned event-level likelihood

PCAT can sample an unbinned likelihood through a user callback. The maintained unbinned_gaussian_mixture example passes the 140 simulated event coordinates directly to pcat.fixed.sample_fixed_chains and sums their Gaussian-mixture log densities with no spatial bins or count map. It samples the four center coordinates of two equal-weight Gaussian components. The component count and width are fixed, so this callback demonstrates inference within one model.

The native typeexpr="gmix" experiment remains the binned Poisson workflow shown in gaussian_mixture_catalog. Its variable-width clusvari elements are fit to an 8-by-8 count grid. boolbinsener=False only indicates that this example has no energy axis. PCAT does not currently provide a built-in unbinned typeexpr="gmix" dispatcher for variable-count mixture components.

Spectral-line likelihood

The one-dimensional typeexpr="fire" workflow uses anlytype="spec" for spectral bins. Set binsenerfull to the monotonically increasing spectral axis edges and use typedata="inpt", strgexprsbrt, typeexpo, and strgexpo for supplied data and exposure. The built-in count likelihood is Poisson by default. liketype="gaus" selects the Gaussian residual likelihood when varidata is supplied. A continuum or background template can be provided through dictfitt["sbrtbacknorm"] and activated with dictfitt["listnamediff"].

The spectype setting selects an analytic spectral shape:

  • "powr" for a power law.

  • "gaus" for a Gaussian profile.

  • "lore" for a Lorentzian profile.

  • "voig" for a Voigt profile.

  • "pvoi" for a pseudo-Voigt profile with mixing fraction frac.

  • "sinc" for a sinc-squared profile.

  • "skew" for a skew-Gaussian profile with shape parameter skew.

  • "toph" for a top-hat profile.

  • "edis" for an energy-dispersion profile using the configured edisintp response.

  • "colr", "curv", or "expc" for color-index, curved, or exponential-cutoff continua.

Line elements use integrated flux flux and line center elin. Gaussian, sinc-squared, skew-Gaussian, and top-hat profiles add sigm. Lorentzian profiles add gamm. Voigt profiles use both widths. Pseudo-Voigt profiles also use frac. Set parameter bounds with limtparaelem and proposal scales with stdvpropelemfire.

Line-spread function

Set lsftype="gaus" and lsfresolvingpower to convolve each line at a constant instrument resolving power. Set lsftype="tabu" and pass an odd-length, nonnegative lsfkernel for a measured line-spread function. Both paths preserve sampled line flux. The default lsftype="none" leaves the intrinsic profiles unchanged. Parameter bounds are supplied through limtparaelem and within-model step scales through stdvpropelemfire.

The voigt_spectral_line_catalog example demonstrates the built-in Voigt profile on simulated spectra. jwst_miri_ngc7027_line_catalog applies the same binned count likelihood to measured MIRI flux converted to effective Poisson counts using its uncertainties and calibration floor. The simulated example also accepts --profile for intrinsic line shapes and --lsftype none|gaus|tabu for instrument broadening. For example, --profile pvoi --lsftype gaus --lsf-resolving-power 3000 fits a pseudo-Voigt line catalog with constant-resolving-power broadening. The response-dependent edis profile is selected through the Python configuration API with an instrument edisintp callable.

Binned photometric time-series likelihood

Use typeexpr="fire" and anlytype="spec" for a time-binned photometric series, with time-bin edges in binsenerfull and observed counts/exposure configured as for other supplied one-dimensional data. This is the same one-dimensional binned likelihood used for spectra. Flare and spot profiles are alternative element models within this likelihood. Fixed baselines can be supplied with dictfitt["sbrtbacknorm"] and enabled with dictfitt["listnamediff"].

Flare spectype options are "flargauss", "flarexpd", "flarfred", and "flardav". They sample peak amplitude flux, peak time elin, and profile-specific widths: fwhm for Gaussian and Davenport profiles, scalfall for one-sided exponential decay, and independent scalrise/scalfall for FRED. Set physical bounds with limtparaelem and proposal scales with stdvpropelemfire. The variable_number_stellar_flares example accepts --profile with any of these four models. For example, --profile flardav selects the Davenport template. The generated time series remains FRED-injected, so alternate fits compare model misspecification against the same data.

Periodic Gaussian spot dips use spectype=["spotrot"] with the lghtlinevoig element container, plus spot_period_days and spot_reference_time_days. Spot depth, phase epoch, and width use the element parameters flux, elin, and fwhm. The rotation period is fixed. See variable_number_stellar_spots for a complete simulated example.

Radial-velocity likelihood

pcat.radial_velocity.retr_dictpcatrvel configures the dedicated Gaussian likelihood for irregular stellar RV observations. Pass observation times time in BJD minus the stated offset [day], velocities rvel [m/s], reported uncertainties stdvrvel [m/s], and integer instrument labels indxinst. The helper sorts observations, removes duplicate epochs, builds time-bin edges, and returns configuration for a variable catalog of lghtlinekepl Keplerian elements. Each planet uses flux for semi-amplitude K, elin for period, phas for mean anomaly, ecce for eccentricity, and argp for argument of periastron.

Set maxmnumbplan for the catalog-size limit, minmrvsa/maxmrvsa and minmperi/maxmperi for amplitude and period bounds, and maxmecce for the eccentricity ceiling. Per-instrument velocity offsets and an optional linear trend are marginalized analytically. Enable the trend with boollinetren=True. Stellar jitter is marginalized on the log-uniform grid listjittrvel, configured through minmjitt, maxmjitt, and numbjitt. The helper also supplies a data-informed period/amplitude/phase birth density and its matching Hastings correction. Its proposal can be tuned with numbperi, expodchi, fracunif, fracgaus, stdvlogtrvsa, and stdvphas. See variable_number_exoplanets_radial_velocity for a multi-instrument example.

Transit-timing likelihood

For transit-time data, use pcat.time_series.log_likelihood_transit_times inside a fixed-dimensional PCAT likelihood callback. The pcat.time_series.make_transit_time_likelihood factory connects a forward predictor to PCAT’s (parameters, data) callback. The data contain transit epochs, observed times, and positive timing errors. The Gaussian likelihood is uncertainty-weighted, up to a parameter-independent normalization constant, and returns negative infinity for nonfinite model times. Ephesos supplies linear, combined sinusoidal-TTV, and optional N-body time predictions. PCAT handles parameter priors and posterior sampling through sample_fixed or sample_fixed_chains. The predictor must align observed epochs with model epochs. See transit_timing_variations for a posterior-sampling example.

Generic user-supplied likelihood

Use typeexpr="gener" for inference within one model with a custom likelihood. The retr_llik(gdat, strgmodl, values) callback returns one log-likelihood value for the supplied parameter vector. PCAT handles configured priors, proposals, accept/reject steps, persistence, and saved sample summaries. Use this path when none of the built-in binned likelihoods matches the data model. See Capabilities for a complete callback example and Sampling, proposals, and convergence for proposal and convergence controls.
